video_title: Playing With Young Luka, Morant & LaMelo Ball Break Down | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on his decision to leave the Cincinnati area
quotes.excerpt: I just didn't want to stay in Cincinnati that bad, but when I think about it, I'm like, you got to work on just what you want.
quotes.quote: I thought I was Superman. I literally thought I was Superman. I just didn't want to stay in Cincinnati that bad, but when I think about it, I'm like, you got to work on just what you want. It was the stupidest shit. I could have just slapped and then woke up at 7:00 to do it, but I just didn't feel it. I didn't feel it. I had to get up out of there.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on his legacy and reception in Columbus
quotes.excerpt: I think sometimes it's not even so much fanboy, it's more than it's like support, love and you know just appreciation.
quotes.quote: I think with Columbus, people show a lot of love. They still show a lot of love. I think sometimes it comes down to, I don't know if it's legend more so than just love. People watch you grow up type of stuff. So I think sometimes it's not even so much fanboy, it's more than it's like support, love and you know just appreciation. Some of those moments where, you know, college times you revert back to it. So I think when people see me, they just think of the shot or think of some of the stuff I did. So it's who's really even a legend, right? You go stand next to Jason Tatum and you feel like you're a loser. Andre Iguodala, like you know what I mean? I used to ragdoll Joe Mazzulla and now he's a man. Like, do you know what I mean? What does it matter? It's just a bald uniform.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Kyrie Irving's decision to return to the Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: I had asked him there, I'm like, why'd you decide to do it before a random preseason game?
quotes.quote: I remember because it was a week or two after Kyrie made the pledge to come back, and I had asked him there, I'm like, why'd you decide to do it before a random preseason game or a random scrimmage, whatever it was. And he's like, I just felt it in that moment. And six months later, the feeling went away.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the evolution of Kyrie Irving's energy
quotes.excerpt: I know Kyrie is different, but he is way different now than then, almost like night and day.
quotes.quote: I know Kyrie is different, but he is way different now than then, almost like night and day in regards to just like energy. Not even breaking up anything negative, but it was like, man, that was back when Kyrie was so full of shit. Do you understand what I'm saying?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Kyrie Irving's desire for independence in Dallas
quotes.excerpt: He didn't ask to be traded to Boston, he was looking for some independence to be able to make his own decisions.
quotes.quote: In his defense, he didn't ask to be traded to Boston, he was looking for some independence to be able to make his own decisions. And I think since then, I mean, Brooklyn didn't end the way he wanted to, but Dallas has been like, I don't know how it's going to end up in Dallas because they're on different timelines, but it just seems to have been like a hand-in-glove kind of fit for him down there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Mike Conley's value as a teammate
quotes.excerpt: Mike Conley might be the best guy in the NBA, the best human being, great teammate.
quotes.quote: For people that don't know, Mike Conley might be the best guy in the NBA, the best human being, great teammate. Still got a little bit of game left obviously, you know, didn't in Minnesota, he kind of faded from the starting lineup, but locker room wise, his value is immeasurable.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on his cover story regarding Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: My cover story on Luka Doncic is out in the magazine on stands this week.
quotes.quote: My cover story on Luka Doncic is out in the magazine on stands this week, online of course, obviously right now.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on his first experience playing against Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: I remember I was playing for the Boston Celtics, this is back in the preseason of 2015.
quotes.quote: I remember I was playing for the Boston Celtics, this is back in the preseason of 2015. So this is before Isaiah Thomas really blew up, but you knew who he was. So we go play Milan, Milano, I think that was Alistair and all those guys. We played them in Italy, and we came over to Madrid. So we knew Real Madrid would be like a better team. I forgot who was really on that team. We handled business. But I remember at the end of the game, Brad's like, yo, there's a 16-year-old coming in. That kid 16, he's pretty good. He's a big like guard. But we were kind of fed up with the whole, you know, every time you do the preseason, it's a Euro conversation. And Milan was saying they were going to beat us, they beat them by 40, and we were like, bro, we don't want to hear any more hype train on anybody. Y'all then brought up Alistair, he hoops like another black kid from the city. For whatever reason, we keep losing spots to all these random guys. So when we saw Luka, it was at the end of the game. I don't know if Avery picked him up or wanted like maybe it's Terry Rozier, but maybe it was even Marcus Smart, but it was somebody that was on him where it's like, yo, he didn't look the same, but the game was over.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Luka Doncic's early professional career
quotes.excerpt: He signed I think 13, 14 years old, I should know I wrote it, but he signed when he was really young.
quotes.quote: He signed I think 13, 14 years old, I should know I wrote it, but he signed when he was really young and he's basically been a pro his entire life, it's crazy.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on Luka Doncic's pace and defensive challenges
quotes.excerpt: When you play with a pacer, jerky, you can kind of comprehend how to guard somebody.
quotes.quote: When you play with a pacer, jerky, you can kind of comprehend how to guard somebody. So when I first seen him, I was like, damn, I see how he's messing people up because his pace is at a crazy level. But I'm like, how the hell did he learn how to do this? The walk up on you, switch his hip, go this way, go that way. And then it's like, yo, he's if he goes left, he's going to step back, but it's like he then threw you off so much, he then hit you with like the little piece of skin on his funny bone and now you're like, you know what I mean? And it's just he was man, he was 19. I just remember leaving and I remember Dame just like, man, this boy cold. I remember Mo and Chief, like man, we just guarded this little ass kid, this boy cold. Like, you know what I mean? And God bless him.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Philadelphia 76ers' turbulent week
quotes.excerpt: Philadelphia, which has had like a pretty turbulent week. You had Ariel Helwani getting hurt out for the season.
quotes.quote: Philadelphia, which has had like a pretty turbulent week. You had Ariel Helwani getting hurt out for the season with an Achilles tear, that cost them a backup center. You also had a little bit of off the court drama when, um, Mike Breen, who you never would think would be involved in something like this. Mike Breen says on the air that somebody told him that Joel Embiid was a couple of minutes late and LeBron got into him. Uh, because of that, LeBron came out and denied it all, said that never happened. Nick Nurse, uh, basically said that didn't happen.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the inevitable drama surrounding LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: I think the hoopla around LeBron, especially in that, naturally, I think the hoopla around LeBron is always some type of quote unquote clunky.
quotes.quote: I think the hoopla around LeBron, especially in that, naturally, I think the hoopla around LeBron is always some type of quote unquote clunky. Then you mix that in with natural Philadelphia media. It's going to be a drama or circus show just in little things because I just feel as though that's brotherly love how how how Philly media is. I think one thing that occurs is, uh, it's just just just adults are alphas trying to figure out how to work together and it's under a huge spotlight.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the 76ers' need for defensive wing depth
quotes.excerpt: I think you need maybe a defensive wing more. And then I think Wade can space the floor as well.
quotes.quote: I think you need maybe a defensive wing more. And then I think Wade can space the floor as well. But I think his defensive presence might be more valuable to them in situations than one of these top guys that's out there.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the 76ers' need for defensive wings
quotes.excerpt: I actually think that someone like Dean Wade might get minutes in those situations.
quotes.quote: I actually think that someone like Dean Wade might get minutes in those situations because Dean Wade in the playoff last year for the Cavs, he was consistently guarding the top wings on the other teams. And look, I think LeBron can still dial it up and be a good defender. Jalen is a good defender. Um, Maxie, Edgecomb, like Embiid, I still need to see how his lateral movement looks like. I think if you need like it's you have all this offensive firepower and I agree you do need some spacing, but I think you need maybe a defensive wing more.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the MVP race and Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: The MVP early predictions, is it Victor Wembanyama's award to lose?
quotes.quote: The MVP early predictions, is it Victor Wembanyama's award to lose? We had some debuts this week in guards. We got Job Morant and Dame Lillard starting out in Portland, Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball in Minnesota.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on Victor Wembanyama's MVP potential
quotes.excerpt: I think Victor Wembanyama, and not for anything just because he's able to do it.
quotes.quote: I think Victor Wembanyama, and not for anything just because he's able to do it. He can play 100 different ways. He has his experience of seeing everything in the NBA. And I don't think it was so much explain well last year, but I think when you move LeBron into that third option like JJ Redick did, it's like, hey, this has nothing to do with you getting the third moves. It's like, sometimes the most the best player, the alpha, is going to sacrifice and fill in the role that's needed.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Bulls' direction
quotes.excerpt: We're in Chicago, so we got to talk a little bit about the Bulls and see what direction they're going.
quotes.quote: We're in Chicago, so we got to talk a little bit about the Bulls and see what direction they're going.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Bulls' roster construction
quotes.excerpt: I actually think that someone like Dean Wade might get minutes in those situations.
quotes.quote: I actually think that someone like Dean Wade might get minutes in those situations because Dean Wade in the playoff last year for the Cavs, he was consistently guarding the top wings on the other teams.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the Bulls' need for floor spacing
quotes.excerpt: Towns alone, even when you go off the street to Orlando Magic, say if they figure out their small ball.
quotes.quote: Towns alone, even when you go off the street to Orlando Magic, say if they figure out their small ball. I feel as though eventually, just knowing the history of Embiid, his knees, his endurance, say he doesn't get it together, that's your liability right there maybe. That's who you go after every single time. And then you're sitting there pointing.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the importance of Joel Embiid's defensive role
quotes.excerpt: I want him to be an elite rim protector as much as I need him to be like a 25 point per game scorer.
quotes.quote: I want him to be an elite rim protector as much as I need him to be like a 25 point per game scorer. I think his defensive presence might be more valuable to them in situations than one of these top guys that's out there.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the Bulls' need for a dangerous small-ball lineup
quotes.excerpt: Whoever has a dangerous small ball, I love it.
quotes.quote: Whoever has a dangerous small ball, I love it. And your small ball right now starts with a 6'6" Josh Giddey, a do-it-all. I think with the team he has, when you sit there, it gets off the board, kick it out to Norman Powell. Norman Powell, NBA All-Star, 20-plus points per game, 40 percent from the three. He knows how to fit into a new team, right? He goes to Miami, plays at an All-Star level. Just a higher gun. You go further, let's do Matas. I know Matas is still developing as an on-the-ball playmaker, but just even getting out in open transition, and looking back in the day, not like a Dwyane Wade or Zach LaVine, but to have that freedom when a healthy Zach LaVine was pushing, that was unbelievable.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Josh Giddey's experience and fit
quotes.excerpt: Josh Giddey is 23 and in year six, I think. He's been a pro since he was 17.
quotes.quote: Josh Giddey is 23 and in year six, I think. He's been a pro since he was 17.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on Caleb Williams' potential and development
quotes.excerpt: I think Caleb Williams is going to be very, very good in that situation.
quotes.quote: I think Caleb Williams is going to be very, very good in that situation. And then when you look at Nick Claxton as a starter, I thought Buddy Hield was a pretty good add-on. But the number one thing that occurs is their small ball, but then also defensively what they could be able to do. I think they could be very, very dangerous in this situation where it becomes a matchup problem or you have a young team that's like, what's the most dangerous about them? They have endurance and it's like you might not be able to catch them. They're going to get out and run.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the Bulls' recurring seasonal struggles
quotes.excerpt: The only thing that throws me off every single year is almost like they get to a point around December and January.
quotes.quote: The only thing that throws me off every single year is almost like they get to a point around December and January and they're always like, well, we tried our best and we do this and we do that. But I think it's about time, you know, they have a standard, they have demands and they try to go out and make the most of it. And I think this off-season signing has really set it because they got a pretty good eight or nine. It's just the East is so deep.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Bulls' need for patience with Caleb Williams
quotes.excerpt: It's going to take Caleb a while to figure it out.
quotes.quote: I think with this group you don't want to have too high expectations. It's not exactly a reset because a lot of the guys are still there, but it's going to take Caleb a while to figure it out. He's going to have great games, but he is young, he is thin, he is going to take some bumps along the way.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner compares the Bulls to the Hornets
quotes.excerpt: We kind of have energy towards the Charlotte Hornets. What's the difference between the Charlotte Hornets and the Bulls?
quotes.quote: I want to compare them right now because I don't know why you feel after they lost some, but we kind of have energy towards the Charlotte Hornets. What's the difference between the Charlotte Hornets and the Bulls? Aren't they kind of similar in that sense?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Hornets' deliberate rebuilding strategy
quotes.excerpt: The Hornets took a deliberate step back. I think they sold high on LaMelo Ball.
quotes.quote: The Hornets took a deliberate step back. I think they sold high on LaMelo Ball. They obviously sold high on Miles Bridges and they're building now on Nick Smith Jr. and Brandon Miller. So they're kind of in that same spot.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix questions the role of Matas Buzelis
quotes.excerpt: Is he the guy that can be the number two option on your team?
quotes.quote: You mentioned Buzelis. Like what is he? Is he the guy that can be the number two option on your team or is he better equipped as three or four? He had a breakout year last year. He was fantastic, but is he going to be the number two guy on your team scoring the ball, playing power forward?

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner on the Bulls' need for intentionality with Buzelis
quotes.excerpt: That starts with being intentional even more in regards to the system and the lineup.
quotes.quote: That starts with being intentional even more in regards to the system and the lineup. I think he did a great job last year. They were running stuff through him, but more so running sets for him. That's where I start looking at, is he the number two guy? Meaning, hey, it's going to be a 20 percent usage rate and we're going to run four or five plays a quarter, maybe four or five plays a half for him as opposed to the little cutsey kid stuff where we're no longer getting our head beating in and he's putting up 25 just because.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on whether Buzelis is a foundational player
quotes.excerpt: I want to see is he worth, is he the guy you build around as your number two?
quotes.quote: That's the thing too. I want to see is he worth, is he the guy you build around as your number two?
